candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: provide medication education and recognize adverse effects and precautions.
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients taking doxycycline that photosensitivity may cause exaggerated sunburn and that direct sunlight or ultraviolet exposure should be limited according to the product warning.

options.A: Doxycycline can cause photosensitivity with an exaggerated sunburn reaction.
options.B: Doxycycline predictably causes permanent skin discoloration in every client exposed to sunlight.
options.C: Sunlight prevents doxycycline absorption, so exposure makes each dose ineffective.
options.D: The advice is only for comfort because doxycycline has no clinically important skin or light-related adverse effects.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed labeling warns that tetracyclines, including doxycycline, can cause photosensitivity manifested by an exaggerated sunburn reaction and advises limiting sun exposure. B overstates tissue hyperpigmentation as universal and sun-dependent. C is not a labeled mechanism. D contradicts the photosensitivity warning.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Doxycycline can cause photosensitivity with exaggerated sunburn reactions and patients should limit sun exposure.
candidate.source_document_title: Doxycycline Hyclate Delayed-Release Tablets Prescribing Information
candidate.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions, Section 5.3 Photosensitivity: photosensitivity manifested by an exaggerated sunburn reaction has been observed with tetracyclines; limit sun exposure. Adverse Reactions also lists photosensitivity.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client taking doxycycline asks why the nurse recommended limiting direct sunlight and using protective measures outdoors. Which response is most accurate?
